case_name: M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra

pages.text:
REPORTABLE
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 330 OF 2021

M/S NEEHARIKA INFRASTRUCTURE PVT. LTD. ... APPELLANT
VERSUS
STATE OF MAHARASHTRA AND OTHERS ... RESPONDENTS

JUDGMENT

M.R. SHAH, J.

1. The core issue before this three-Judge Bench relates to the scope and power of the High Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) and Article 226 of the Constitution of India in passing interim orders of 'no coercive steps' or staying arrest during the pendency of quashing petitions.

2. Police have the statutory right and duty under Section 156 and relevant provisions of the Code to investigate into a cognizable offence. The courts should not thwart any lawful investigation into cognizable offences.

3. An interim order staying investigation or directing that no coercive steps be taken should be passed only in exceptional cases where the FIR does not disclose any cognizable offence. In petitions under Section 482 CrPC, High Courts should not pass blanket interim orders staying arrest or investigation without recording cogent reasons.
